record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
record.original_question: Is the following characterization true: an Archimedean triangular norm T is 1-Lipschitz with respect to the L_p norm if and only if every additive generator of T is the p-th power of a convex function?

evidence.quote: Each continuous Archimedean t-norm T can be represented by means of a continuous additive generator.
Conjecture 3.2. An Archimedean t-norm T is 1-Lipschitz with respect to the L_p-norm if and only if each of its additive generators is a p-power of a convex function.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A triangular norm (t-norm) is a binary operation $T:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ that is commutative, associative, non-decreasing in each argument, and satisfies $T(x,1)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. A t-norm $T$ is called Archimedean if it is continuous and $T(x,x)<x$ for all $x\in(0,1)$. Every continuous Archimedean t-norm admits a representation $T(x,y)=t^{(-1)}(t(x)+t(y))$ via a continuous additive generator, i.e. a continuous strictly decreasing function $t:[0,1]\to[0,\infty]$ with $t(1)=0$, where $t^{(-1)}$ is the pseudo-inverse of $t$.

For $p\in[1,\infty)$, the t-norm $T$ is said to be $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L_p$-norm if
$$\bigl|T(x_1,y_1)-T(x_2,y_2)\bigr|\;\le\;\bigl(|x_1-x_2|^p+|y_1-y_2|^p\bigr)^{1/p}$$
for all $x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2\in[0,1]$.

A function $f:[0,1]\to[0,\infty]$ is said to be the $p$-th power of a convex function if there exists a convex function $g:[0,1]\to[0,\infty]$ such that $f(x)=g(x)^p$ for all $x\in[0,1]$.

Decide whether the following characterization holds: an Archimedean t-norm $T$ is $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L_p$-norm if and only if every additive generator of $T$ is the $p$-th power of a convex function.
artifact.status_search_result: The characterization appears to have been established in subsequent work on $k$-$l_p$-Lipschitz t-norms, where Archimedean $1$-$l_p$-Lipschitz t-norms are shown to be exactly those whose additive generators are $p$-convex (equivalently, $p$-th powers of convex functions), with necessary and sufficient conditions provided.

status_evidence.title: k-lp-Lipschitz t-norms
status_evidence.snippet: Archimedean k-lp-Lipschitz t-norms are characterized by means of k-p-convexity of their additive generators; necessary and sufficient conditions for a function to be a k-p-convex additive generator are given.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured characterization is confirmed: an Archimedean t-norm is 1-l_p-Lipschitz iff its additive generators are p-convex (p-th powers of convex functions).
